main_concerns.concern: The evidence is still a set of file references and command summaries. A referenced excerpt/hash file is a receipt, not proof, unless its content is shown; the scoped git status intentionally excludes the broader worktree; and 'decision=optional' from the gate is ambiguous and weaker than explicit authorization.

The anti-loop boundary is declarative (text in a markdown file), not structural (a contract, check, or gate that blocks further plan-only edits). The lifecycle packet still returns decision=optional and nothing in the system will mechanically reject another round of plan refresh. However, given the explicit task constraint "Do not implement runtime code in this task," a structural anti-loop cannot be built within this scope — the declarative boundary is the strongest available mechanism, and it is now explicit where it was previously absent.

minimum_fixes.minimum_fix: Inline the excerpt, hash, and execution mapping; provide a full worktree git diff or equivalent no-runtime-change verification; and explain the gate decision value so its authorization is unambiguous.

No further plan edits are needed. The next step should implement one item from the execution mapping — create or update a single contract, connect a single check, or modify a single runtime path — and submit that implementation for Prism review. This is consistent with the plan's own anti-loop boundary and will produce verifiable evidence (a git diff with code changes) rather than another closeout artifact.
